task.description:
Investigate GH #596 (ISS-0627, MAJOR): the remainder of GH-594/ISS-0626's handoff bookkeeping debt after the safe-mechanical subset was fixed -- 292 findings across 6 categories that each need either case-by-case judgment or a permanent-acknowledgment decision, per ISS-0627's own acceptance criteria: H003 (148 BLOCKER, unrecoverable timestamp inversions), H004 (34 BLOCKER, same problem opposite direction), H013 (53 BLOCKER, computable whole-hour offset but unrecorded timezone), H005 (5 BLOCKER, no completed_at to recover), H009 (38 MAJOR, orphaned pipeline steps -- marking COMPLETED would fabricate evidence), H001 structural-typo subset (~4 files, per-file bracket/delimiter judgment), H006 CONDITIONAL (1 finding, needs a real enum decision), H007 (69 findings / ~10 files, early alternate schema needing an explicit migration decision).

ISS-0627's own acceptance criteria already say 'this is deliberately NOT a single run -- expect this to be split further per category as each is tackled, following the same phased-issue pattern used for ISS-0624/ISS-0625.' Your job is to make that split concrete for THIS run:

1. Read docs/issues/ISS-0627.json in full (already has substantial detail from the prior triage -- do not re-derive from scratch, build on it).
2. Assess which SINGLE piece is the right scope for this one WF-03 run. Consider: the acknowledgment-mechanism design (for H003/H004/H005/H009 -- a genuinely new, well-scoped capability: a dated, reasoned suppression/acknowledgment marker keyed by handoff_id+code, so these ~225 findings stay visible as KNOWN historical gaps rather than either being silently re-flagged forever or fabricated shut) is likely the highest-value, lowest-risk piece to tackle first, since it unblocks the largest finding count (225 of 292) without requiring any per-file content judgment -- but verify this assessment yourself rather than assuming it's correct. The remaining categories (H013's timezone-correction policy decision, H001-structural's ~4 individual bracket fixes, H006-CONDITIONAL's single enum decision, H007's ~10-file schema-migration decision) are smaller and more naturally suited to individual, later runs since each is a distinct judgment call rather than a shared mechanism.
3. If you agree the acknowledgment mechanism is the right scope for this run: design what it needs to look like at a diagnosis level (do not implement) -- e.g. where does the acknowledgment record live (a new file under docs/ or handoffs/? fields needed: handoff_id, finding code, dated, reasoned justification, who/what acknowledged it), and exactly how tools/lint_handoffs.py's full-corpus scan (not just --changed mode, which GH-594 already fixed) should treat an acknowledged finding differently from an unacknowledged one (e.g. still counted and listed, but under a distinct 'ACKNOWLEDGED' bucket rather than BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR, so it never disappears from visibility but also never blocks a gate it shouldn't). This must NOT weaken the underlying detection --  every one of the 225 findings must still be individually recorded and visible, just categorized as 'known and accepted' rather than 'red'.
4. If you disagree with the acknowledgment-mechanism-first assessment, propose and justify a different single-piece scope for this run instead.
5. File any necessary follow-up issues for the pieces this run does NOT cover (if not already adequately covered by ISS-0627's existing text), and route to CODE-DESIGNER with your finalized scope. Do not implement anything yourself.
acceptance_criteria: Single, concrete scope decision made for this run (acknowledgment mechanism, or a justified alternative)
If acknowledgment mechanism chosen: record shape and lint_handoffs.py integration approach diagnosed, not implemented
Underlying detection is never weakened -- every finding remains individually visible
Routed to CODE-DESIGNER with the finalized scope, not implemented directly
Any pieces not covered by this run remain clearly tracked in ISS-0627 for future runs

result.summary:
Re-verified GH-594's own handoff's suggestion that the acknowledgment mechanism (for H003/H004/H005/H009) is the right first piece of ISS-0627's 292-finding remainder, against a fresh full-corpus run of tools/lint_handoffs.py (no --changed): 250 BLOCKER + 110 MAJOR + 1 MINOR across 2275 handoffs, per-code breakdown H003 148 / H004 34 / H005 5 / H009 38 / H013 53 / H007 69 / H006 1 / H001 9 / H008 3 / H010 1 -- matches ISS-0627's snapshot within the small drift expected from GH-594's own commits since the original triage. CONFIRMED the assessment: of the 6 remaining categories, H003/H004/H005/H009 (225 of 292 findings) are the only ones that share a genuine, reusable MECHANISM need (a permanent, auditable record that a specific unrecoverable-timestamp or orphaned-step finding has been reviewed and accepted as known history, not fixed or hidden) -- H013 needs its own timezone-correction policy decision, H001-structural needs per-file delimiter judgment (~4 files), H006-CONDITIONAL needs one specific enum decision read from that file's own context, and H007 needs an explicit schema-migration-vs-recognize-old-shape decision (~10 files). None of those 4 benefit from being bundled with the acknowledgment mechanism or with each other.

Scoped this run to designing (not implementing) the acknowledgment mechanism for H003/H004/H005/H009 only, and routed to CODE-DESIGNER (handoff 06e8f858-2ef9-4fad-8798-5a631d3c8e19) with a diagnosis grounded in prior art already present in this exact codebase rather than a novel design, found by reading tools/lint_test_wiring.py, tools/lint_test_isolation.py + its baseline.json, and tools/lint_test_tenant_provisioning.py + its baseline.json:

1. STORAGE + KEY-MATCHING: tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json's content-keyed shape (severity|code|file|line|message, matched via issue_key()/load_baseline() at lines ~313-345 of lint_test_isolation.py) is the closest existing analog. Verified that lint_handoffs.py's H003/H004/H005 finding messages already embed the actual timestamp values (f-string interpolation of started/completed/created), so a message-text-inclusive key means a genuinely new or changed finding on the same file cannot silently match an old acknowledgment for a different finding -- this satisfies the handoff's requirement #4 (don't let a gate silently stop measuring new defects) without needing a separate content-hash field. Flagged one open question for CODE-DESIGNER to verify: whether H009's message (which embeds a count and run_id rather than a timestamp) could ever produce two distinct orphan situations with byte-identical messages on the same file, which would need a stronger key.

2. BUCKET/EXIT-CODE SEMANTICS: tools/lint_test_wiring.py's KNOWN_UNATTACHED ledger already establishes the exact precedent CLAUDE.md asks for -- a distinct 4th bucket ([KNOWN]), individually printed every run, explicitly excluded from the failure count, with the comment 'EMPTY, and that is the intended steady state' proving this codebase already treats such ledgers as visible accepted-debt registers, never as silent suppression. Directed CODE-DESIGNER to reuse this bucket semantics (a new ACKNOWLEDGED bucket alongside BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR, excluded from the counts['BLOCKER'] or counts['MAJOR'] exit-code check) but NOT its small-scale dict-literal storage, since 225 entries need the file-based baseline approach instead.

3. AUDITABILITY OF THE MECHANISM ITSELF: tools/lint_test_tenant_provisioning.py's --no-baseline flag and 'Suppressed N issue(s) from baseline' print line is the right CLI convention to carry over so the acknowledgment mechanism can itself be validated by running without it.

4. PROVENANCE: tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json's header fields (version/generated_at/source/regenerated_by/regeneration_note) give the WHO/WHEN/WHY shape CLAUDE.md and ISS-0627 ask for, but at file-level granularity. Left an explicit open design question for CODE-DESIGNER: whether 225 entries need individually distinct reason text (tedious, likely repetitive noise since all 225 share exactly 4 root causes already fully explained in ISS-0627) versus one shared per-category rationale plus a single generation-run header -- recommended the latter but required the design doc to state the choice explicitly rather than default silently.

5. GENERATION MECHANISM: directed CODE-DESIGNER to design a reviewed one-time script (parallel to the existing tools/repair_handoff_bookkeeping.py precedent from GH-594) that imports and reuses lint_handoffs.py's own _lint_parsed_handoff/lint_orphans detection functions -- not a reimplementation of the predicates -- to mechanically emit one baseline entry per currently-existing H003/H004/H005/H009 finding, reviewed once as a script + dry-run diff, not by hand-typing 225 entries.

6. EXPLICITLY REQUIRED the design to keep this mechanism distinct from --changed mode's existing preexisting_file_finding_codes/preexisting_run_finding_codes diff logic added in GH-594 -- that logic answers 'did this branch introduce this finding' (compares branch vs merge-base); this new mechanism answers 'has this specific historical finding been reviewed and permanently accepted' (compares against a curated baseline file). The two must compose, not merge: a file can be outside --changed's scope and still have some findings acknowledged and others not.

Explicitly scoped OUT of this run and left for individual future runs, unchanged in ISS-0627: H013 (53 BLOCKER, timezone-offset-correction policy decision), H001-structural (~4 files, per-file delimiter judgment), H006-CONDITIONAL (1 finding, needs the file's own context read by hand), H007 (69 findings / ~10 files, schema-migration decision). Updated docs/issues/ISS-0627.json's notes field with this run's scope decision and verification so future runs picking up the remaining 4 categories have a clear record of what was and was not covered here. Did not touch tools/repair_handoff_bookkeeping.py's existing GH-594 scope. No implementation performed -- Step 2 (CODE-DESIGNER) produces the design doc; Step 2b (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR) reviews it before BACKEND-DEV implements.
